subject: science
question:
The diagram shows a cross section of the top layers of the Earth. There are three colors in the legend. Gray is lithosphere. Orange is asthenosphere. Blue is ocean. Not noted in the legend is the color of the sky which starts at darker blue and fades to lighter blue until it reaches a line labeled Sea Level. There are three structures noted in the diagram: Island, Mid-Ocean Ridge, and Continent.
Island has an orange core starting above sea level down through the to an orange layer. The orange core is surrounded by gray. At the gray level, there is an arrow that points to the left.
Mid-Ocean Ridge is all below sea level. There is a gray level surrounding an orange core. There is a small opening where the orange meets the blue level below sea level.
Continent starts above sea level. It has a gray mound with a vertical orange line. At sea level another mound of gray where the orange vertical line widens then narrows before it widens to just below the gray layer. There is an arrow that points to the right.
Which statement best explains the tectonic plates that carry the continent and the island are moving away form each other as shown in the diagram?
choices: Gravitational force between the Sun and Earth is breaking up the plates.
Convection currents in Earth’s mantle are pulling the plates in opposite directions.
Magnetic materials in Earth’s mantle is pulling each plate into a subduction zone.
Water currents in the ocean are pushing the ocean floor in opposite directions.
answer: B. Convection currents in the Earth's mantle are pulling the plates in opposite directions.

picture.description: Cross section of lithosphere and asthenosphere with an island, a mid-ocean ridge and a continent; arrows show the plates moving apart.

The second method, washing the soil, involves digging up the contaminated soil; washing it on site with a water solution containing nitric acid; capturing the wash solution containing the dissolved lead nitrate that is produced by the reaction of nitric acid and lead; removing the lead nitrate from the water and disposing of it; and returning the treated soil to the ground. The third method is growing mustard plants in the soil. Mustard plant that absorb lead from the contaminated soil are grown; the plants are harvested, then dried and burned on site. The lead is reclaimed from the ash produced by burning the plants. Six to eight crops of mustard plants are grown and harvested until the lead is reduced to a safe level.]
All of the treatment methods described will successfully reduce lead to safe levels. Each method has environmental advantages and disadvantages.
In the table below, identify one environmental advantage and one disadvantage specific to each method.
[Figure: Image of a table with space to enter the environmental advantage and disadvantage of removing the soil, washing the soil, and growing mustard plants in the soil.]
